summary: A candidate whom Pindrop calls “Ivan X” applied for a remote engineering role and advanced from résumé screening to a video interview on 18 February 2025. Pindrop said the candidate’s video showed unnatural facial movements and audio lag, and its detection tool flagged a face swap. Pindrop described a second interview eight days later under the same identity with a different apparent face. The company identified the application as fraudulent; the available account does not say Ivan X was hired or passed its interview identity check.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Full active taxonomy 0.6.7 re-adjudication removes FC-000046. Its recognition requires an inferential or verification state to be treated as sufficient authority for a consequential action without the independent basis. Ivan X passed initial résumé screening but Pindrop detected the face swap in the interview; no hiring, authorised access or binding identity acceptance is established. FC-000079 Economic Solicitation Authenticity is not established because this record does not evidence a payment or comparable economic solicitation attributable to this applicant. FC-000053 generator-side identity authority is unknown. The attempt remains an Incident with no established canonical failure class.

classification_review_provenance.method: record-by-record full taxonomy 0.6.7 review and direct targeted-party source check
classification_review_provenance.reviewer: OpenAI Codex / GPT-6 under human-directed VIGIL governance
classification_review_provenance.authority_boundary: FC-000046 failed its consequential authority condition because Pindrop reports detecting, rather than accepting, the synthetic candidate at interview. FC-000079 and FC-000053 lack distinct required evidence. No human verification of raw interview telemetry is asserted.

assessment_boundaries: Pindrop’s account is first-party reporting by the targeted company; raw interview material and its detection telemetry were not independently tested here.
Advancement to interview and a later coding assessment do not establish that identity checks were passed or that employment was offered.
The Guardian article covers a broader pattern, not additional consequences caused by Ivan X.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The AI Incident Database entry identifies an attempted deepfake job application at Pindrop. Pindrop’s first-party account places Ivan X in an interview, describes visible anomalies and says its tool confirmed the suspected face swap. A later Pindrop account says the screening interview was on 18 February 2025 and its real-time assistant flagged the video; it also reports a subsequent coding assessment, which should not be mistaken for verified identity or hiring. The Guardian article concerns a wider pattern of AI-assisted remote hiring and does not prove a different outcome for Ivan X. No employment, payroll access or downstream compromise is established.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The attacker-facing attempt used AI-mediated appearance to obtain a credible candidate presentation. In the observed Pindrop process, the face swap was flagged during interview and did not become sufficient identity authority for hiring. The record therefore cannot support the previous failure-occurrence mapping that said the synthetic applicant passed the consequential verification boundary. It remains a bounded attempted deception and detected boundary, with no established downstream employment or access effect.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: Synthetic identity can carry an application past an initial résumé screen, but that step is distinct from authorising employment or system access. This occurrence shows an interview-stage detection and illustrates why the identity evidence, each decision gate and the outcome need separate reporting.
